title: NoSQL
body:
A family of databases that don't use the relational table-and-schema model — document stores like [[MongoDB]], key-value stores like Redis and DynamoDB, wide-column and graph databases. Flexible mixed-shape items on the shelf rather than a strict predefined layout.

The usual trade: you give up schema enforcement, [[JOIN]]s, and often strict transactional guarantees, and you get flexibility, easier horizontal scaling, and a shape that maps directly onto [[JSON]] documents. Related data tends to be embedded or duplicated rather than joined, which makes reads fast and updates awkward. The honest interview answer to "SQL or NoSQL?" is that it depends on whether your data is genuinely relational and how much you need the schema to protect you — and that modern Postgres has good [[JSON]] support, so the line is blurrier than it was. Either way it's a **database server**, distinct from and usually on a different machine than the app server.
